examples.problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
y' = 2x - y, \qquad y(1) = 0
$$

Use the trapezoidal method with one step to approximate $y\!\left(\dfrac43\right),$ rounded to two decimal places.
examples.worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
y' = f(x,y), \qquad y(a) = c,
$$

the trapezoidal method with step size $\Delta x$ is given by

$$
\Delta y = \dfrac12(y' + y'_\text{new}) \cdot \Delta x,
$$

with $y'_\text{new} = f(x_\text{new}, y_\text{new})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

First, since we want to find the value of $y$ at $x=\dfrac43,$ we will use a step size of

$$
\Delta x = \dfrac43 - 1 = \dfrac13.
$$

Now, let's proceed with the trapezoidal method. In general, $\Delta y$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(2x-y+(2{x}_{\text{new}}-{y}_{\text{new}}))\cdot \frac{1}{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}(2x-y+2{x}_{\text{new}}-{y}_{\text{new}}) \\  & =\frac{1}{6}(2x-y+2{x}_{\text{new}})-\frac{1}{6}{y}_{\text{new}}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute this into $y_\text{new} = y + \Delta y{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+\frac{1}{6}(2x-y+2{x}_{\text{new}})-\frac{1}{6}{y}_{\text{new}} \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{1}{6}(2x+2{x}_{\text{new}}+5y)-\frac{1}{6}{y}_{\text{new}}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we solve for the general formula for $y_\text{new}{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{7}{6}{y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{1}{6}(2x+2{x}_{\text{new}}+5y) \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{1}{7}(2x+2{x}_{\text{new}}+5y)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, in the first step, the new $x$ value is $x_\text{new} = 1 + \dfrac13 = \dfrac43.$ Hence, the new $y$ value is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{1}{7}(2x+2{x}_{\text{new}}+5y) \\  & =\frac{1}{7}(2\cdot 1+2\cdot \frac{4}{3}+5\cdot 0) \\  & =\frac{2}{3} \\  & ≈0.67.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that $y\!\left(\dfrac43\right) \approx 0.67.$

feedback.problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=4x-5y,\,y(-2)=1
$$

The trapezoidal method is applied with step size $Δx=5.$ Find the general formula for the new $y$ value, ${y}_{\text{new}},$ in terms of the current values $x$ and $y,$ and the new value ${x}_{\text{new}}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,y(a)=c,
$$

the trapezoidal method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
Δy=\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx,
$$

with ${y}_{\text{new}}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{\text{new}})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

In this example, $Δy$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(4x-5y+(4{x}_{\text{new}}-5{y}_{\text{new}}))\cdot 5 \\  & =\frac{5}{2}(4x+4{x}_{\text{new}}-5y)-\frac{25}{2}{y}_{\text{new}}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute this into ${y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+\frac{5}{2}(4x+4{x}_{\text{new}}-5y)-\frac{25}{2}{y}_{\text{new}} \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{5}{2}\,(4x+4{x}_{\text{new}}-\frac{23}{5}y)-\frac{25}{2}{y}_{\text{new}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for the general formula for ${y}_{\text{new}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{27}{2}{y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{5}{2}\,(4x+4{x}_{\text{new}}-\frac{23}{5}y) \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{5}{27}\,(4x+4{x}_{\text{new}}-\frac{23}{5}y) \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{1}{27}(20x+20{x}_{\text{new}}-23y)\end{aligned}
$$
